title: Chong Ho Yi v. Korean Capital Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC approved the Panel’s recommendation declaring the case administratively out of order because the complainant did not file a complaint after Presbytery addressed the case at a called meeting.
first_summary: The SJC declared Chong Ho Yi’s case against Korean Capital Presbytery administratively out of order because he did not file a complaint after Presbytery dealt with the case at a called meeting. The sparse notice gives no merits ruling or further relief.
summary: A complainant failed to file a complaint after Korean Capital Presbytery dealt with his case at a called meeting. The SJC therefore approved the Panel’s recommendation declaring the matter administratively out of order. The notice provides no ruling on the underlying dispute and states no further relief or proceedings.

sources.supports: Case identity, SJC adoption, administrative disposition, and the failure to file a complaint.

evidence_notes.dispute: Line 9 identifies the procedural defect: no complaint was filed after Presbytery acted at a called meeting.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Line 9 declares the case administratively out of order for that filing failure.

evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision is incorporated by reference; line 9 directly reports the adopted Panel recommendation.
